findings.governingReading: Shirou specifically dislikes making a child younger or smaller than himself suffer.
findings.explanation: The English drops the comparison to Shirou that makes his protectiveness relational rather than an abstract rule.

findings.evidenceJa: 残りのマスターと決着がつくまで
findings.governingReading: Shirou offers shelter until matters with the remaining Masters are settled.
findings.explanation: Until the end removes the concrete endpoint and leaves what must end unspecified.

findings.highlight: I get her off of me[line2]well, there’s no need to do that myself as Saber does it for me.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺がするまでもなく、セイバーが引き離してくれていた
findings.governingReading: Before Shirou can separate Illya from himself, Saber does it for him.
findings.explanation: The run-on first assigns the removal to Shirou, then retracts it after the fact; the source gives Saber uninterrupted agency.

findings.governingReading: Saber says sheltering Illya has a hundred harms and not a single benefit.
findings.explanation: Only bring harm preserves the negative verdict but omits the emphatic denial of any benefit.
